 South Carolina Football: Suddenly Unstuck 
 SPORTS South Carolina Football: Suddenly Unstuck
 The Gamecocks are on a heater as South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer’s squad continues flipping the script on its 2026 season… 
 by Will Folks November 8, 2026 November 11, 2026 4 
 by WILL FOLKS 
 *** 
 A little over a month ago, long-suffering South Carolina football fans realized they were stuck with Shane Beamer – an underperforming, sixth-year head coach whose regressing program was mired in a massive, multi-season slump.
 Dating back to a December 31, 2024 bowl loss to Illinois , Beamer’s teams had dropped twelve of their last eighteen games through early October of this year – posting an anemic 1-10 mark against conference opponents along the way. Calls were intensifying for the head coach’s head – including one originating from this author – but it soon became clear the program lacked the $24 million necessary to pay his buyout.
 More accurately, the program didn’t have the money to pay Beamer’s massive buyout, purchase the contracts of his staff and hire a top-tier replacement (along with his assistants)… especially seeing as its biggest donor passed away just day before the season started.
 South Carolina was stuck… not unlike the last time it fired a head coach .

 *** 
 At its moment of peak desperation, though, something improbable happened. South Carolina traveled to the Swamp in Gainesville on October 10 and emphatically knocked off then-No. 16 Florida – reminding fans (and perhaps the team itself) what it was capable of achieving. Two weeks later, following a bye, the improbable happened again – with Beamer’s squad downing then-No. 11 Tennessee at home.
 Suddenly out of their own way – and out of their own heads – the Gamecocks found themselves on a heater.
 The past two Saturdays, South Carolina recorded two more conference wins, first on the road over Oklahoma – a decisive Halloween hammer drop – and next against Texas A&M , a gritty homecoming victory which came despite star quarterback LaNorris Sellers nursing an ankle injury. While the Sooners and the Aggies were both unranked, each team entered the season in the Top Ten – and those two games (like Florida and Tennessee before them) projected as likely losses for the Gamecocks following their abysmal start to the season.
 South Carolina’s disastrous first five games – which included a blowout loss to Alabama and the surrender of double-digit leads in losses to Mississippi State and Kentucky – portended another losing campaign for Beamer.
 Now, that inauspicious start seems like ancient history…
 *** 
 *** 
 With Sellers leading the way, South Carolina has reeled off four straight victories against conference opponents and is now ranked No. 20 in the Associated Press’ Top 25. They could climb even higher when the latest College Football Playoff ( CFP ) rankings are released this Tuesday (November 10, 2026) at 9:00 p.m. EST.
 During South Carolina’s winning streak, Sellers has thrown for 1,041 yards and nine ( 9 ) touchdowns – he’s also rushed for 246 yards and another six ( 6 ) scores, resoundingly reinserting himself into the Heisman Trophy conversation. In fact, former Gamecock head coach (and 1966 Heisman winner) Steve Spurrier has already indicated Sellers has earned his vote for the award.
 Saturday’s gutsy performance against the Aggies likely earned the Florence, S.C. native some additional support from Heisman voters across the country with three games remaining in the regular season.
 Injured late in the first half, Sellers limped through most of the second stanza against Texas A&M – severely limited in his ability to run the football and also adversely impacted in his throwing motion in certain situations. With South Carolina’s 6-foot-3, 238-pound superstar seemingly confined to just one of his two dimensions (and top tailback Matt Fuller out of the lineup with a broken foot) the Gamecock offense grew predictable – and predictably sputtered in the second half.
 *** 
 South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers celebrates his team’s 17-9 victory over Texas A&M at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 7, 2026 ( @GamecockFB/X ) 
 *** 
 Thankfully, coordinator Clayton White ‘s defensive unit collectively stiffened during the fourth quarter against an Aggie offense that amassed 457 yards in a losing effort. The pivotal stop occurred when linebacker Justin Okoronkwo and edge rusher Anthony Addison combined for a 14-yard sack of quarterback Marcel Reed on fourth down with just 1:27 on the clock.
 On the very next snap, Sellers made the play of the Gamecocks’ season – a read option surprise that caught defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill ‘s troops completely by surprise. With all eleven Aggies – and all 78,687 fans in attendance at Williams-Brice Stadium, for that matter – expecting the Gamecock signal-caller to hand the ball to tailback Jabree Coleman , he instead plucked it from his teammate’s breadbasket and sprinted around the right end of Texas A&M line. Caught off guard by the injured quarterback’s sudden burst of speed, Aggie linebackers and defensive backs were left in the proverbial dust as Sellers raced 41 yards for a touchdown.
 The erstwhile hobbled No. 16 hopped the final five yards to pay dirt… 
 *** 
 His moment. https://t.co/idW3doRjnw
— South Carolina Football (@GamecockFB) November 8, 2026 
 *** 
 While there was initial concern after his teammates had to help him off the field following his game-clinching touchdown, Sellers is expected to suit up for South Carolina’s upcoming game against Arkansas ( 3-6 , 1-5 SEC ) next Saturday in Fayetteville.
 “We fully expect him to play,” Beamer told reporters on Sunday. “Right now, it’s nothing that concerns us aside from his pain tolerance and getting some of the swelling down in that ankle.”
 With the Gamecocks’ win on Saturday, Beamer’s team is now bowl eligible for the fourth time during his tenure. With a win next Saturday over the Razorbacks, Beamer could secure his fourth winning season in six years. South Carolina also has an outside chance to qualify for the CFP if it can run the table the rest of the regular season – although beyond next weekend’s road win it would have to defeat No. 1 Georgia at home and arch-rival Clemson on the road on Thanksgiving weekend to accomplish that feat.
 With the recent winning streak Beamer has improved to  39-33  ( .541 ) overall during his tenure in Columbia – with a  20-27  ( .425 ) mark against conference opponents and a  9-23  ( .281 ) record against ranked foes.
 For those of you keeping score at home, the longest winning streak in South Carolina football history is ten ( 10 ) games – achieved between November 12, 2011 and October 13, 2012 under Spurrier. The Gamecocks’ longest winning streak under Beamer is 2024’s six-game run.
